result.title: LEAP: Efficient LLM Inference Scheduling with Generalizable Length Prediction
result.summary: Length-aware scheduling reduces request latency in LLM serving by prioritizing shorter requests. However, despite their large model sizes, length predictors can suffer degraded ranking performance under domain and task shifts, and adapting them can require costly retraining. Their prediction overhead can further offset the benefits of scheduling. To improve the generalization and efficiency of length-aware scheduling, we propose \textbf{LEAP}, a length prediction system with fast online adaptation and asynchronous CPU execution. LEAP reuses the serving model's prefill hidden states, which contain information about the output length, and extracts this signal through a linear readout. To adapt to substantial domain and task shifts, it updates the readout at test time through recursive least squares, using completed requests as supervision without gradient computation or historical-data replay. Prediction and updates run asynchronously on CPU, while prediction and initial batch ordering overlap the remaining GPU prefill. Across the evaluated cross-domain transfers, LEAP retains strong ranking performance, and online adaptation improves Spearman correlation by 64.7\% under a larger domain shift. Serving experiments show that LEAP reduces average per-token latency by 15.9--40.8\% compared with the evaluated length predictors, while achieving 1.9\% higher throughput with $30{,}569\times$ fewer predictor parameters than the strongest evaluated baseline.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 LEAP 长度预测系统：复用服务模型 prefill 阶段的隐状态，通过线性读出预测输出长度，并用递归最小二乘在测试时以已完成请求为监督在线更新；预测与更新异步运行于 CPU，与 GPU prefill 重叠，用于长度感知调度。
AI.relevance_reason: 「从 prefill 隐状态线性探针读出输出长度」加「无梯度在线更新」可供核查 LVR 中 latent 状态的读出方式与停止/长度决策的测试时自适应，但论文目标是服务调度而非推理机制，联系需人工判断。
